_comment: Weight registry. Weights are NOT stored in this repository: a weight swap
used to look like an ordinary source edit, which is how a good checkpoint
once got quietly overwritten. Everything here is identified by hash and
fetched on demand into a local cache.
Run `python scripts/prepare_release.py` to recover the archived weight,
strip optimiser state, write the release assets and fill in the 'sha256'
fields below. Until that has been done a null sha256 means 'unverified'

source.note: Archived in git history; recoverable with `git cat-file blob <blob>`.

notes: Default weight. This is the one the tool has always been used with.
Its training data is used to build an embedding model that feeds an
unsupervised clustering step. That data's licence constrains use in a
synthesis path; this is not a synthesis model. The boundary is stated
plainly here rather than left implicit. Choose timbre-alt-v1 if you
want a weight with no such caveat.

source.note: The filename said 1570000 but the checkpoint's own step counter reads 165000.

notes: Cleaner licensing provenance, noticeably weaker separation in practice.
Kept so the choice is available and explicit.
The upstream encoder, trained for speaker identity rather than timbre
style. It answers a different question: use it to tell singers apart,
not to separate one singer's registers. Same architecture, so it loads
safetensors is preferred over pytorch_model.bin: it loads by tensor
name with no unpickling, which is also why the emotion trunk is
implemented in-tree instead of through transformers.
